# The route parameter binding is allocated against the handler's own locals.
#
# `sess`, `ok`, `s`, `id`: an href used to be able to claim any of them, since
# the parameter's name was a placeholder the program wrote, and only `w` and
# `r` had been prefixed out of the way. `{s}` was the worst, because it
# rewrote a signature rather than a statement --
# `func renderHandlePage(s *handlePageState, s string) string`.
#
# The name is the window declaration's now, not the program's: the params
# arrive as one struct bound to the slot's own parameter. So there is one name
# to allocate around rather than one per placeholder, and a program that wants
# `s` in its path gets a field called `s`, which is nobody's local. The
# reservation stays because the declaration may rename the binding, and that
# is a breaking change to callers rather than to this file.
#
# This has to compile, not parse: a redeclaration is valid Go syntax, so
# `format.Source` accepted it and `sngl generate` exited 0.

sngl generate --lang go --platform html -o out app.sngl

exec go build ./...

# The struct's fields carry the names the path wrote, the handler's locals are
# untouched by them, and the binding is what the render function takes.
grep 'v.S = __r.PathValue\("s"\)' out/server.go
grep 'v.Id = __r.PathValue\("id"\)' out/server.go
grep 'id, ok := snglSessionID' out/server.go
grep 'renderHandlePage\(s, v\)' out/server.go

-- go.mod --
module paramname

go 1.24

-- srv/srv.go --
package srv

func Bump(n int) int { return n + 1 }

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import "go:paramname/srv"
import "sngl:platform/html"

struct PageParams {
    id string
    s string
}

var hits = 0

window #page(title="t", href=`/p/{id}/{s}`, params=PageParams{}) {
    html.button(innerText="go", @click { hits = srv.Bump(hits) })
    html.span(innerText="{v.id}{v.s}{hits}")
}
